analysis:
The PR only modifies CHANGELOG.md (documentation, lines 11-808 on head). There is no executable code in the supplied evidence, so it adds no direct security regression. I read all three units (metadata, two patch hunks) against the threat model.

The changelog describes features whose security properties could not be verified from this diff and need review when the code lands:
- Two-Mac cluster pairing and registration (TB-002, TB-011, T-053, T-054). It describes the coordinator-derived approvals and the cluster_runtime block in registration, and the member-role registration. The changelog says approvals are derived from releases and that member grants follow hardware-only capabilities. The authorization binding, revocation and stale-grant handling are outside the supplied evidence.
- Cluster link control channel and model copy over Thunderbolt. This includes the pairing-keyed encrypted records, the manifest-digest pinning, and the refusal of hard links, unexpected files and occupied destinations. It is new attack surface that the threat model does not yet cover (TB-003, A-004). The weight-substitution threat T-012/T-027 applies to the pinned-manifest repair path, which rewrites manifest.json in place after fetching it from the CDN or coordinator.
- The local API listens on every network interface by default for `darkbloom cluster local`, authenticated by an API key shared with `darkbloom start --local`. A relay on the non-rank-0 Mac was also added. This is new network exposure that the threat model does not describe.
- Per-tenant prefix cache on the pair, with a SHA-256 digest of the cache scope on both ranks and SSD records. This relates to T-041/SEC-035. Requests from the local endpoint carry no partition and keep the earlier shared behavior. Cross-tenant sharing is therefore unchanged for local use.
- The pair SSD prefix tier, which stores records with quantized latents. It is new at-rest artifacts under the T-041 scope: records are scoped by artifact, build and MTP policy, but no TTL or HMAC-naming statement for these records is visible in the changelog.
- The changelog states that provider.toml is now owner-only, that the updater uses umask 022, and that failure-handling changes remove the retry of response_format truncation. These are positive or neutral.
- Cluster failover to solo serving, and leader claims travelling only over the keyed link channel (availability and spoofing). These need code-level review.

No finding is raised, since the diff contains no code. The next pass should examine the cluster code paths named above once they are supplied. needs_deeper_review is true because the changelog describes substantial new trust boundaries (cluster link, LAN-exposed local API, pair SSD cache) whose implementation was not supplied.
